name: particles-component-cpu
title: Particles PR-B: ParticleSystem component, IParticleBackend seam, CPU backend and billboard rendering
issue: particles-gpu-probe (#122) is merged: `physics.gpu` off|auto|on (default off), GpuStatus via IPhysicsBackend, the Particles health row (states Running/Disabled/Failed), Physics.IsGpuAvailable(); on Linux the GPU is Unavailable. Re-read the merged code (engine/include/engine/physics/GpuStatus.hpp, IPhysicsBackend.hpp, PhysXBackend, Application.cpp health rows) and the proposal first. The health Particles row from PR-A reflects the PhysX GPU probe only; with this item it must also say which backend a ParticleSystem is using when one exists (CPU or PhysX) without breaking PR-A tests. Decisions: orchestrator/proposals/physx-particles.md (Decisions block): one ParticleSystem component with `backend: Auto | PhysX | CPU`; Auto = PhysX when the GPU probe is Ready, else CPU; CPU billboards rendered through UpdateMesh; no protocol change (backend is an ordinary component field). Scope (PR-B, fully CI-verifiable, runs headless): (1) engine/include/engine/physics/IParticleBackend.hpp: CreateSystem(desc)->handle, Spawn(handle, positions, velocities), SetParams, Destroy, CopyPositions(handle, std::vector<Vec4>&), obtained from IPhysicsBackend::GetParticleBackend() (nullptr by default). (2) A CPU particle backend (no PhysX): emitter (rate, burst, lifetime, start speed/size/color ranges, gravity scale, cone/sphere shape), integration in the fixed step, simple collision against the physics world via raycast/sphere checks only if cheap and optional (otherwise ground plane only; document), deterministic with a seed, capped max particles with a clear warning. (3) ParticleSystem component modelled on Light/TextRenderer: fields, serialization, reflection/inspector (no protocol change; verify GetComponentTypes exposes it and an enum field `backend`), registration, Lua access (engine/src/scripting/bindings/LuaComponentBindings.cpp ~l.109 pattern) plus Play/Stop/Clear/EmitBurst(n), play-mode rules (particle state is never serialized, exit play clears, pause freezes via timeScale 0). (4) Rendering: camera-facing billboards rebuilt on the CPU each frame through UpdateMesh on the OpenGL and software renderers (Vulkan is still stubs: no-op there with a one-time warning), additive/alpha blend setting, texture optional. The `backend` selection: PhysX with no PhysX backend/GPU falls back to CPU with one warning (health row from PR-A stays truthful); the PhysX backend itself is PR-C and is NOT in this item. (5) Tests: simulation determinism, caps, serialization round trip, Lua API, backend selection/fallback, billboard mesh generation, headless run (no window), software-renderer golden image if the existing test pattern supports it. (6) docs/ (a new particles section/page linked from the docs index), README mention.
acceptance: All Tests-workflow jobs green on all legs including headless Linux (particles run on the CPU backend there)
A scene with a ParticleSystem round-trips through save/load and play mode
